questions.question: What is angular displacement?
choices: Distance along a straight path regardless of rotation
Change in tangential speed
Change in the rotation axis's mass
Change in rotational position measured as an angle

questions.question: What is angular velocity?
choices: Rate of change of angular position
Rate of change of mass
Force multiplied by time
Energy divided by distance

questions.question: What is torque?
choices: The linear speed of every point on a wheel
The turning effect of a force about an axis
The mass of an object multiplied by temperature
The amount of charge stored in a battery

questions.question: What does rotational inertia describe?
choices: The rate at which angular position changes
The turning effect of an applied force
Resistance to changes in rotational motion
The total number of turns in one second

questions.question: Which SI unit is commonly used for torque?
choices: Kilogram per meter
Watt per second
Meter per second
Newton-meter

questions.question: What is angular acceleration?
choices: Rate of change of angular velocity
Rate of change of circumference
The radius of a rotating body
The total number of rotations ever completed

questions.question: What is angular momentum?
choices: The torque required to start an object from rest
A quantity describing rotational motion that can be conserved
The distance traveled by a point in one turn
The tangential speed at the object's center

questions.question: Why is it easier to open a door by pushing far from the hinges?
choices: The same force produces less torque but greater angular speed
The door's rotational inertia changes when the push position changes
The same perpendicular force produces greater torque
Only a push close to the hinge can cause angular acceleration

questions.question: How does moving mass farther from a rotation axis affect rotational inertia?
choices: It reduces inertia because the axis is farther away
It leaves inertia unchanged if total mass is unchanged
It changes angular velocity without any relation to inertia
It generally increases it

questions.question: Two points on a rigid spinning disk have different radii. Which quantity is the same for both?
choices: Angular velocity
Tangential speed
Distance traveled in one turn
Centripetal acceleration

questions.question: Why does an isolated skater spin faster when pulling in the arms?
choices: Rotational inertia increases while angular momentum stays fixed
Rotational inertia decreases while angular momentum is conserved
Pulling in the arms creates a net external torque by itself
Angular momentum increases while rotational inertia stays fixed

questions.question: When is angular momentum conserved for a chosen system?
choices: Whenever its angular speed is zero
Whenever its mass is nonzero
When net external torque is zero
Only when it has no kinetic energy

questions.question: How is rolling without slipping different from sliding?
choices: The whole wheel is instantaneously at rest
The contact point slides forward at the center's speed
The wheel's center remains at rest while the rim turns
The contact point is instantaneously at rest relative to the surface

questions.question: What happens when equal opposite torques act on a rigid body about one axis?
choices: Net torque is zero, so angular acceleration is zero
The body must immediately stop rotating
Rotational inertia becomes zero
The body must rotate faster

questions.question: Why can a spinning object have constant angular speed but moving points still accelerate?
choices: Their speed magnitude must increase every turn
Their velocity directions change as they circle
Their velocity directions remain constant
Only changes in speed magnitude count as acceleration

questions.question: A perpendicular 10 N force acts 0.4 m from a pivot. What torque does it produce?
choices: 25 N·m
4 N·m
40 N·m

questions.question: A wheel makes 6 complete rotations in 3 s. What is its rotation rate?
choices: 18 rotations/s
0.5 rotations/s
9 rotations/s
2 rotations/s

questions.question: A rigid disk spins steadily. Point B is twice as far from the axis as point A. How do their tangential speeds compare?
choices: B is twice as fast as A
Their speeds are equal
B is half as fast as A
B is four times as fast as A

questions.question: Angular velocity increases from 2 rad/s to 10 rad/s in 4 s. What is the average angular acceleration?
choices: 3 rad/s²
2 rad/s²
8 rad/s²
32 rad/s²

questions.question: Two identical masses rotate about an axis. In one arrangement they are close to it; in the other they are farther away. With equal applied torque, which accelerates more rapidly?
choices: The arrangement with masses farther away
Both must have identical angular acceleration
The arrangement with masses closer to the axis
Neither can accelerate
